questions.stem: What is the concentration of a solution?

options.text: The total volume of the solution
The amount of solute dissolved in a given volume of solution

questions.explanation: Concentration is the amount of solute dissolved in a given volume of solution. It can be measured in g/dm³ (grams per cubic decimetre) or mol/dm³.

questions.stem: What is the formula for concentration in g/dm³?

options.text: Concentration = Mass of solute (g) / Volume of solution (dm³)

questions.explanation: Concentration (g/dm³) = Mass of solute (g) / Volume of solution (dm³). This tells you how many grams of solute are dissolved in each dm³ of solution.

questions.stem: 10 g of salt is dissolved in 500 cm³ of water. What is the concentration in g/dm³?
questions.explanation: First convert 500 cm³ to dm³: 500/1000 = 0.5 dm³. Concentration = 10/0.5 = 20 g/dm³.

questions.stem: How many cm³ are in 1 dm³?
questions.explanation: 1 dm³ = 1000 cm³. This is also equal to 1 litre. To convert cm³ to dm³, divide by 1000.

questions.stem: A solution has a concentration of 40 g/dm³. What mass of solute is in 250 cm³ of this solution?
questions.explanation: 250 cm³ = 0.25 dm³. Mass = Concentration x Volume = 40 x 0.25 = 10 g.

questions.stem: If you add more water to a solution, what happens to the concentration?
questions.explanation: Adding more water (solvent) increases the volume but keeps the amount of solute the same. Since concentration = mass/volume, increasing the volume decreases the concentration (the solution becomes more dilute).
